name: Potion Belt
description: The quick-use owner for consumables, not a second inventory. Core Inventory and Slotted Bag own storage and quantities; the belt validates a use, removes exactly one accepted item, starts its shared cooldown, and emits typed recovery, status, and cleanse requests. It never applies healing, changes a resource pool, or mutates status itself. Authored definitions support self or explicit-unit targeting, always or out-of-combat use, shared cooldown groups, flat/percent-max/full recovery, status applications, and cleanse rules. Every explicit inventory.useRequested carries a stable useId; accepted and rejected ids are remembered and exact replays are silent no-ops. Rejection for an unknown item, empty stack, wrong target, combat policy, or active cooldown consumes nothing and starts nothing. Derived recovery, application, and cleanse ids are stable functions of useId and operation index, so downstream owners can dedupe independently. Cooldown timers have per-user/group generations, and stale completion cannot clear a newer cooldown. Legacy input.potionSlot and the effects map retain their prior immediate heal behavior; id-less legacy calls do not gain a fabricated cross-save dedupe guarantee. Restoring quantities, cooldowns, generations, and processedUseIds emits no historical use, recovery, status, cleanse, or cooldown events.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: beltSlots
inputs.description: Quick-use slots. Four is a real constraint: health, mana, utility, and one slot the build argues about.

inputs.name: autoRefillFromBag
inputs.description: Whether the next stack of the same potion slides into the slot when one empties. Manual refill is hardcore; auto is the genre default.

inputs.name: useCooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Minimum gap between sips. Without it, a full stack is a health bar with extra steps.

inputs.name: effects
inputs.description: What each consumable does, as {itemId: {heal?}} — item data, which the descriptor says this component does not decide, handed in by the request. An item absent from the map is not a potion and never reaches the belt. `heal` is applied to the player's unit through combat.unit_roster's heal.

inputs.name: definitions
inputs.description: Authored consumables: {id, targetMode self|unit, usePolicy always|outOfCombat, cooldownGroupId, cooldownSeconds, consume, recovery?, statusApplications?, cleanseRequests?}. Recovery operations are {resourceId, mode flat|percentMax|full, amount?}; health goes to Unit Roster and other named pools go to Resource Pools. Status and cleanse entries reference Status Effects definitions and rules.

inputs.name: initialState
inputs.description: Restored active cooldowns, timer generations, processedUseIds, and last rejection. Inventory quantity is restored by its storage owner, not copied into the belt.

outputs.name: beltContents
outputs.description: Item id and stack count per slot.

outputs.name: potionsRemaining
outputs.description: Total across all belt slots, for the HUD counter.

outputs.name: effectOf
outputs.description: What drinking a carried kind would do — {heal} — or null for a thing that is not a consumable here. The inventory panel asks.

outputs.name: activeCooldowns
outputs.description: Live per-source cooldown groups with remainingSeconds, timerId, and generation.

outputs.name: processedUseIds
outputs.description: Durable accepted and rejected explicit-use dedupe ledger.

outputs.name: lastRejected
outputs.description: Latest rejected use with useId, itemId, targetId, and reason unknownItem|empty|invalidTarget|inCombat|cooldown|invalidRequest.
